thread.title: Dow Drops 14 Points as Semiconductors Keep the Nasdaq Afloat

title: Dow Drops 14 Points as Semiconductors Keep the Nasdaq Afloat
text:
Dow Drops 14 Points as Semiconductors Keep the Nasdaq Afloat By Updated Jan. 24, 2019 3:18 p.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
3:16 p.m. A quick glance at the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite tells you that something is going very right for the tech heavy Nasdaq that isn’t for the blue-chip benchmark . And that thing is semiconductor stocks.
The iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) is up 6% at $170.49, helping keep the Nasdaq afloat—it’s risen 0.6% to 7070.43. The price-weighted Dow’s one chip stock is Intel (INTC), which has gained 4.1% to $49.95, but its low price means that it doesn’t contribute much to the Dow’s up or down moves, especially when Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and International Business Machines (IBM)--$100-plus stocks, each—are all down on the day. As a result, the Dow has dipped 14.12 points, or 0.1%, to 24,561.50.
Semi’s are rallying thanks to strong earnings from Texas Instruments (TXN), up 6.9% at $102.07, and STMicroelectronics (STM) Lam Research (LRCX), Xilinx (XLNX), and Teradyne (TER), which have all gained more than 10% . “Semis were supposed to be out of favor, weren’t they?” Bespoke investment Group’s Paul Hickey asked rhetorically in a note released Thursday morning. “That’s not the case this morning.”
Or this afternoon, for that matter. The group, which was pretty much left for dead at the end of 2018, suddenly looks very much alive.
